html:
Tatev Monastery is a monastery on the edge of a deep gorge in Syunik in southern Armenia, whose main church was built from 895 to 906. In the late 1300s and early 1400s it ran one of the main universities of medieval Armenia.

Its scholars, led by Gregory of Tatev, taught theology, philosophy, grammar, music and painting, and copied and illuminated manuscripts, many now kept in the Matenadaran. Tatev was also a large landowner and the seat of the bishops of Syunik. It was sacked by Seljuks and by Timur's armies. A cable car opened in 2010, among the longest of its kind, carries visitors across the gorge. It is a symbol of the scholarly tradition of Armenia.
